Function: CaptureGroup.public CaptureGroup(string jpegPath, string rawPath, string? xmpPath = null)
Rationale: Ctor rejects null/blank jpegPath, rawPath and non-null xmpPath via ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace; Array.AsReadOnly caches (ImagePaths/Paths) are built once so callers cannot mutate them; jpegPath==rawPath is not rejected but no producer can create it (Build keys by extension, RestoreMembers uses Build). No direct ctor-throws test found (exercised via CaptureGroupBuilderTests/CaptureAndEntryMutationGapTests).

Hand-written Equals(CaptureGroup?) compares the three paths OrdinalIgnoreCase and null-safe (null XmpPath == null XmpPath); needed because compiler record equality would compare the cached arrays by reference. Checked other==null. Tests: CaptureGroup_EqualsNull_IsFalseWithoutThrowing, Equals_SamePathsIgnoringCase_AreEqualWithSameHashCode, Equals_DifferentRawOrSidecar_AreNotEqual.

HashCode.Add with OrdinalIgnoreCase for all three paths is consistent with Equals (equal-ignoring-case groups hash equal; null XmpPath hashes as 0). Tests: CaptureGroup_SamePathsInDifferentCase_AreEqualWithEqualHashCodes, CaptureGroup_DifferentGroups_HaveDifferentHashCodes.

PreferJpeg/PreferRaw return the member; Separate (and any undefined enum value) throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException, which is correct because Separate never creates groups; all callers (GroupEntries, RestoreMembers, TryReformGroup) are guarded by mode != Separate. No direct unit test of the throwing branch found (covered indirectly by GroupEntries tests).

Returns the cached read-only [Jpeg,Raw] list; never null, same instance each call (Paths_TakenBeforeAChange style tests rely on stability). Used by ReviewCatalog index build and RemovePaths: order JPEG first is what survivor selection in RemovePaths assumes.

Cached [Jpeg,Raw] plus optional Xmp list; XMP appended last so image members are always the first two entries (FileActionService group moves iterate it). Read-only wrapper over a private array: no external mutation.

Function: CaptureGroupBuilder.public static IReadOnlyList<CaptureGroup> Build(IEnumerable<string> imagePaths, IEnumerable<string>? sidecarPaths = null)
Rationale: Checked: null imagePaths throws; blank/non-image extensions skipped; buckets keyed by (dir, basename) OrdinalIgnoreCase with Path.GetDirectoryName normalising separators so C:/a and C:\a pair; a bucket groups only with exactly 1 JPEG (.jpg/.jpeg) and exactly 1 RAW (duplicates or case-variant twins stay ungrouped, which is the safe direction); first-seen order is kept (deterministic). Edited .tif next to RAW is never the JPEG side. Tests: Build_LeavesUnpairedAndAmbiguousFilesSeparate, Build_NonJpegImageNextToRaw_IsNotGrouped, Build_MatchesSameFolderAndBasenameIgnoringCase_AndIncludesXmp.

Function: CaptureGroupBuilder.private static string? ChooseSidecar(Dictionary<CaptureKey, List<string>> sidecars, CaptureKey key, string jpegPath, string rawPath)
Rationale: Checked sidecar choice: exact base-named .xmp wins and two case-variants yield null (no weaker fallback), else exactly one file.ext.xmp among both members, 2+ candidates yield null; early return when no sidecars keeps the 10k-entry hot path allocation-free. Ambiguity means no sidecar is claimed so sidecar stays put on Move/Recycle (documented). Tests: Build_SidecarNamedBaseXmpWinsOverFileExtensionSidecars, Build_TwoCompetingFileExtensionSidecars_AreAmbiguousAndLeftOutOfTheGroup.

Function: CaptureGroupBuilder.public static IReadOnlyList<CatalogEntry> GroupEntries( IReadOnlyList<CatalogEntry> entries, RawPairMode mode, IEnumerable<string>? sidecarPaths = null)
Rationale: Checked: null entries throws, undefined mode throws before any state change, Separate and no-groups return a copy; collapsed entry takes the position of the first member seen and the representative entry (own metadata) with CaptureGroup set; emitted set uses reference equality so one emission per group; representative always present in entryByPath because Build derives groups from these same paths. Duplicate paths (case variants) make the bucket ambiguous so nothing is dropped. Tests: GroupEntries_CollapsedEntryTakesPositionOfFirstMemberSeen_NotTheRepresentative, GroupEntries_UsesSelectedRepresentativeAndKeepsBothMembersAddressable, GroupEntries_TenThousandPaths_GroupsAllPairsWithBoundedAllocation.
Lambda entry => entry.Path projecting the catalog entries to Build; trivial, null entries are filtered earlier in ReviewCatalog.Reset.

Function: CaptureGroupBuilder.private static Dictionary<CaptureKey, List<string>> IndexSidecars(IEnumerable<string>? sidecarPaths)
Rationale: Indexes only .xmp (extension compared OrdinalIgnoreCase) by (folder, name without .xmp) so a.xmp sits under a and a.cr2.xmp under a.cr2; null/blank skipped; same-key duplicates accumulate in the list so ambiguity is detectable by Count. Tests: Build_SidecarThatIsNotAnXmpFile_IsNotAttachedToTheGroup, Build_XmpSidecarWithMatchingName_IsAttached.

Records only the first JPEG path and a count: second JPEG makes JpegCount 2 so the bucket is rejected, never silently picking one of two JPEGs (which could act on the wrong file). Trivial and covered by Build_LeavesUnpairedAndAmbiguousFilesSeparate.
Same first-path-plus-count logic for RAW; ambiguity (two RAWs of one basename, e.g. A.CR2 and A.DNG) correctly leaves the bucket ungrouped. Covered by Build_LeavesUnpairedAndAmbiguousFilesSeparate.

Compares Directory and BaseName OrdinalIgnoreCase, consistent with Windows path semantics and with GetHashCode; struct keys so no allocation. Covered implicitly by Build_MatchesSameFolderAndBasenameIgnoringCase_AndIncludesXmp.
HashCode.Combine of OrdinalIgnoreCase hashes of both parts; consistent with Equals; Directory is never null because Build substitutes string.Empty for GetDirectoryName null.

init accessor re-validates via RequirePath so entry with { Path = blank } throws ArgumentException instead of smuggling an empty path; field keyword backing store. Test: Path_RejectsBlank_ViaConstructorAndWith.

Length and LastWriteUtc must both equal the stat; unknown (null) Length never matches so an unstatted entry is treated as changed (safe). FileStat is a record class but all callers pass a non-null stat. Compared by DateTime ticks (Kind ignored), fine for UTC from FileInfo. Covered via ImagePresenter tests; no direct unit test of Matches found.

Function: CatalogEntry.public CatalogEntry WithMetadata(long length, DateTime lastWriteUtc, int? width = null, int? height = null)
Rationale: Stat unchanged keeps unsupplied width/height, changed stat drops them, supplied dims always win; partial dims (width only) with changed stat leave Height null which is acceptable. Tests: WithMetadata_UnchangedStat_KeepsDimensions, WithMetadata_ChangedStat_DropsOrReplacesDimensions, WithMetadata_SuppliedDimensionsReplaceTheKnownOnesEvenWhenTheStatIsUnchanged. Negative lengths are not rejected (callers pass FileInfo.Length so cannot be negative).

Null, empty and whitespace all throw ArgumentException with paramName path; used by both ctor initialiser and init. Test: Path_RejectsBlank_ViaConstructorAndWith, CatalogEntry_InvalidPath_ThrowsArgumentException.

Function: ComparePairService.public static (string Left, string Right)? Find(IEnumerable<string> files, string path)
Rationale: Legacy per-query pair finder: same folder + extension (OrdinalIgnoreCase), base stem via ^(.*) \(\d+\)$, original = first path-sorted file with the base stem, numbered = the path itself when numbered else lowest-suffix variant. Path.GetFullPath throws on null/invalid chars (callers pass scanned paths). No production caller (ImagePresenter uses BuildIndex); kept as oracle for ComparePairFuzzTests.BuildIndex_MatchesFind and ComparePairServiceTests.
Where predicate: same directory (GetFullPath-normalised, OrdinalIgnoreCase) and same extension; GetFullPath called per candidate is O(n) per Find which is why BuildIndex exists. Oracle only.
OrderBy key GetFullPath with OrdinalIgnoreCase: deterministic path order which defines which file is the original. Oracle only.
ThenBy key with Ordinal breaks ties between case variants deterministically. Oracle only.
FirstOrDefault predicate: stem equals base stem OrdinalIgnoreCase, picks first in sorted order; matches BuildIndex originals.TryAdd. Verified by ComparePairFuzzTests.
selected candidate when the query path itself is numbered and present in the list; if the path is absent the lowest numbered variant is returned instead, which BuildIndex never queries. Oracle only.
Where candidate IsNumberedVariantOf(baseStem) feeding OrderBy(NumberedSuffix) and FirstOrDefault: lowest suffix wins, ties keep path order (OrderBy stable). Oracle only.

Function: ComparePairService.public static Dictionary<string, (string Left, string Right)> BuildIndex(IEnumerable<string> files)
Rationale: Result equals Find for every key (ComparePairFuzzTests.BuildIndex_MatchesFind) and handles duplicates, depth-2 numbering and case-variant folders. Performance: ImagePresenter.GetComparePair rebuilds the whole index on the UI thread at the next key press whenever StructuralVersion changed (every Recycle/Move/Undo), including folders with no numbered files at all. Measured 229 ms for 100k paths (86 ms at 10k incl. JIT) in a scratch program. See W2-CC-05.
Select lambda computing (Path, Full) once per file so GetFullPath is not repeated by the sort comparers; throws on invalid path (scanned paths cannot be invalid).
OrderBy on full path OrdinalIgnoreCase: the order in which originals are chosen and ties resolved; same rule as Find.
ThenBy Ordinal tie-break for case-variant twins; same rule as Find.
GroupBy key (folder, extension) with FolderExtensionComparer (OrdinalIgnoreCase) so DSC0001.JPG pairs with DSC0001 (1).jpg; folder null only for a root path which is never a file.

List.Sort is unstable, so ties on suffix fall back to the position in the already path-sorted list; position dictionary uses TryAdd so duplicate identical paths get the first position and the comparer stays consistent (a, a) == 0.

Comparison lambda: suffix compare then original position; consistent total order (no int overflow because CompareTo, not subtraction). position[a] cannot miss because the dictionary is built from the same list.

Function: ComparePairService.private static bool IsNumberedVariantOf(string candidate, string baseStem)
Rationale: Candidate must be strictly longer than baseStem and match ^(.*) \(\d+\)$ with group1 equal to baseStem OrdinalIgnoreCase. Note \d also matches non-ASCII digits (NumberedSuffix then falls back to int.MaxValue); harmless ordering only. Covered by ComparePairServiceTests and fuzz tests.

Takes the trailing (n) of the stem; int.TryParse failure (huge or non-ASCII digits) yields int.MaxValue so such variants sort last, no exception; int.TryParse without an explicit culture is safe here because the string is digits only. Verified (x (99999999999)) sorts after x (1)/x (2) in a scratch run.

Function: ComparePairService.FolderExtensionComparer.public bool Equals((string? Folder, string Extension) x, (string? Folder, string Extension) y)
Rationale: Folder and extension compared OrdinalIgnoreCase (null folder equals null folder only); consistent with the hash code.

Function: ComparePairService.FolderExtensionComparer.public int GetHashCode((string? Folder, string Extension) obj)
Rationale: Hash combines OrdinalIgnoreCase hashes with null folder as 0; consistent with Equals.
Valid only when Kind is not Invalid AND FolderPath is non-null. Test: DragDropResult_IsValid_NeedsAKindOtherThanInvalidAndAFolder.

Function: DragDropInputService.public static DragDropInputResult Parse(IEnumerable<string>? paths, bool rawEnabled = false)
Rationale: Folder wins over files; images are filtered by File.Exists + IsSupported(rawEnabled) and the first image defines the folder; mixed folders and unsupported files produce the right warnings; null/blank handled. Defect: the same existing folder dropped twice in different spellings (trailing separator) is counted as an ignored path and raises the spurious OnlyFirstFolder warning (reproduced: Parse([d, d+sep]) gives IgnoredPathCount=1 and a warning). Also performs synchronous Directory.Exists/File.Exists per dropped path on the caller thread (UI in MainViewModel.OpenDropped). See W2-CC-06.
Where filter dropping null/whitespace paths so later Directory.Exists never sees them.

Count predicate compares the raw dropped string with the chosen folder using OrdinalIgnoreCase, so a trailing-separator or forward-slash spelling of the same folder is counted as ignored; should compare Normalize()d, separator-trimmed paths. See W2-CC-06.

Where File.Exists and ImageFileTypes.IsSupported(path, rawEnabled): RAW only accepted when RAW support is on; missing files are excluded. Test: ParseUnsupportedFileIsInvalid, DragDropParse_ImageAndUnsupportedFile_CountsTheUnsupportedOneAsIgnoredAndWarns.

Accepted images are those whose normalised directory equals the first image's folder (OrdinalIgnoreCase); images from other folders raise MixedFolders and are counted ignored. Test: DragDropParse_ImagesFromTwoFolders_KeepsTheFirstFolderAndWarnsAboutMixedFolders.

Path.GetFullPath; callers only pass paths that already passed Directory.Exists/File.Exists, so invalid characters cannot reach it; relative paths resolve against the process CWD (drag/drop always supplies absolute paths).

Function: ExplorerReason.public static string Format(string code, params string[] details)
Rationale: Latent: details are joined with | without escaping, so a detail containing | (for example a COM call name or exception text) round-trips as extra details (reproduced: Format(code,a|b) then Parse gives 2 details). Every current caller passes pipe-free text (type names, 0xHRESULT, counts, fixed COM call names) so there is no live failure; params null would throw NullReferenceException. See W2-CC-07. Test: FormatThenParse_RoundTripsCodeAndDetails (no pipe case).

Function: ExplorerReason.public static (string Code, string[] Details) Parse(string reason)
Rationale: Null throws ArgumentNullException; empty string gives code empty with no details; no separator gives itself as code (documented); parts[1..] never throws. Tests: Parse_TextWithoutSeparator_IsItsOwnCodeWithNoDetails, FormatThenParse_RoundTripsCodeAndDetails.

Function: ExplorerSnapshotValidator.public static bool TryValidate(ExplorerViewSnapshot snapshot, IReadOnlyCollection<string> scannedFiles, out IReadOnlyList<string> ordered, out string? reason)
Rationale: Wrapper converts ArgumentException/NotSupported/IO errors from COM-sourced data into IncompleteSnapshot instead of crashing the load (tests: NullPieces_ReturnFalse, InvalidCandidatePath_ReturnsFalse, ExplorerSnapshotValidator_NullSnapshot_IsAnIncompleteSnapshotNotACrash). Defect shared with TryValidateCore: the ordered list returns normalised strings, not the caller's scanned strings, so a catalog whose paths carry the extended prefix is rejected by ReviewCatalog.ReplaceOrder. See W2-CC-01.

Function: ExplorerSnapshotValidator.private static bool TryValidateCore(ExplorerViewSnapshot snapshot, IReadOnlyCollection<string> scannedFiles, out IReadOnlyList<string> ordered, out string? reason)
Rationale: Validation logic is sound (status, null list, folder canonicalisation, per-item empty/outside/duplicate checks, set equality via counts because seen rejects duplicates; sub-folders and non-image files are skipped; Explorer extras are ignored). Defect: result holds NormalizePath(candidate) which strips the \\?\ prefix, while FolderLoadCoordinator passes the scanned strings to ReplaceOrder verbatim; with scanned paths starting with the extended prefix validation returns true but ReplaceOrder returns false, silently dropping Explorer order (reproduced in scratch program). See W2-CC-01.

NormalizePath then TrimEndingDirectorySeparator; a drive or UNC root keeps its separator so C:\ and C: are not confused. Throws for null/invalid (caught by callers). Test: CanonicalizeFolderIsIdempotent, DriveRootFolderIsSupported, UncFolderIsSupportedInBothSpellings.

GetFullPath then strips \\?\UNC\ to \\ and \\?\X: to X:, leaves other \\?\ forms (Volume GUID) untouched; length guard before indexing full[5]. Tests: NormalizePath_StripsTheExtendedPrefixOnlyFromDriveLetterPaths, NormalizePathStripsExtendedPrefixOnly.

Function: ExplorerSnapshotValidator.private static bool InFolder(string normalizedPath, string canonicalFolder)
Rationale: Span-based directory compare avoids per-item allocation, falls back to SamePath so the verdict equals the full comparison (ExplorerSnapshotValidatorEquivalenceTests.MatchesOriginal_OnMutatedSnapshots); root-level files give a directory with trailing separator that equals the canonical root.

Function: ExplorerSnapshotValidator.public static bool SamePath(string first, string second)
Rationale: Compares canonicalised folders OrdinalIgnoreCase; throws on invalid input (callers ExplorerOrderService/WindowSelector wrap in try). Test: CanonicalizeFolderAndSamePathWorkCorrectly.

Function: GenerationClock.public GenerationClock(long initialNavigation = 0, long initialFolder = 0, long initialInteraction = 0)
Rationale: Plain field initialisation of the three counters (negative or long.MaxValue seeds allowed; Interlocked.Increment would wrap at MaxValue which is unreachable). Test: Constructor_InitializesGenerationsToSpecifiedValues.
Volatile.Read of a long field (atomic on x64, Volatile.Read guarantees on 32-bit too). Test: Next_IncrementsMonotonicallyAndUpdatesCurrent.
Interlocked.Increment returns the new value so concurrent callers get distinct tokens. Tests: Next_IncrementsMonotonicallyAndUpdatesCurrent, ConcurrentIncrements_AreThreadSafeAndAccurate.
Volatile.Read equality; a stale token never matches because counters only grow. Covered by GenerationClockTests and the App folder/navigation tests that cancel stale work.
Volatile.Read of the folder counter; independent from navigation/interaction counters by design.
Interlocked.Increment on the folder generation; returned value is the new token. Concurrency covered by ConcurrentIncrements_AreThreadSafeAndAccurate.
Equality check against the volatile folder counter; used by FileActionController/FolderLoadCoordinator staleness checks (R02/R08 findings in WORK-REVIEW concern the callers, not this primitive).
Volatile.Read of the interaction counter.
Interlocked.Increment on the interaction counter.
Equality against the volatile interaction counter.

Three independent Interlocked increments, documented as not one atomic step (a concurrent reader may see navigation advanced before folder); consumers only compare tokens so no inconsistent state is exposed. Tests: StopForAction_IncrementsAllThreeCountersSimultaneously, ConcurrentStopForAction_IncrementsAllCountersWithoutLoss.

Exposes the private HashSet as IReadOnlySet; case-insensitive, exactly eight RAW extensions (test pins them). Callers could cast to HashSet and mutate but nothing in the repo does. Test: RawExtensions_AreExactlyTheEightApprovedFormats.

Span overload uses HashSet.GetAlternateLookup over the OrdinalIgnoreCase comparer (supported on .NET 10) with Path.GetExtension(span) so it is allocation-free; empty extension and dotfiles return false. Test: IsRawPath_StringOverload_HandlesNullAndRawAndNonRawNames (string overload) plus ImageFileTypesTests.
Null returns false, otherwise delegates to the span overload. Test: IsRawPath_StringOverload_HandlesNullAndRawAndNonRawNames.
Delegates with rawEnabled false so RAW files are not supported by default. Test: IsSupportedValidatesExtensions.

Function: ImageFileTypes.public static bool IsSupported(string path, bool rawEnabled)
Rationale: Blank path and extensionless names rejected; case-insensitive set lookup; RAW only when rawEnabled. Does not accept .xmp (handled separately by FolderLoadCoordinator). Test: IsSupportedValidatesExtensions.

Function: ImageSortService.public static List<CatalogEntry> SortEntries( IEnumerable<CatalogEntry> entries, ImageSortMode mode, INaturalComparer? naturalComparer = null)
Rationale: Default keeps enumeration order, NameAscending/unknown enum values use natural name order, NameDescending is the exact reverse of ascending, Size sorts use Length with unknown as -1 then name tie-break (stable OrderBy). Managed comparer path precomputes natural keys (perf) with the identical comparison. Tests: ImageSortServiceTests (12 cases), NaturalSortPropertyTests, SortAndPairMutationGapTests. Production caller: FolderLoadCoordinator.LoadAsync with the default comparer.
Local function Path.GetFileName(entry.Path); returns an empty string for a path ending in a separator which cannot happen for CatalogEntry file paths.
OrderByDescending key entry.Length ?? -1L: unknown size sorts last in descending mode.
OrderBy key entry.Length ?? -1L: unknown size sorts first in ascending mode (acceptable, scan always supplies Length except when stat failed).
Reverses the freshly created list in place (private list so no aliasing); reversing the ascending order also reverses ties, which is exactly the documented NameDescending contract.

Function: ImageSortService.private static IOrderedEnumerable<T> OrderByName<T>(IEnumerable<T> items, Func<T, string?> nameOf, INaturalComparer comparer)
Rationale: ManagedNaturalComparer instance takes the key-caching path whose order equals Compare (same key, case-insensitive, ordinal tie-breaks); any other INaturalComparer uses the generic comparer. Test: ManagedNaturalComparerEquivalenceTests.
Lambda builds one NameKey per item (key computed once by OrderBy, so O(n) key allocations rather than O(n log n)).

Function: ImageSortService.private static IOrderedEnumerable<T> ThenByName<T>(IOrderedEnumerable<T> ordered, Func<T, string?> nameOf, INaturalComparer comparer)
Rationale: Same key-caching logic for ThenBy after a size order; ties keep stable order.
Lambda building the NameKey for the secondary sort.
Null name yields a null key; otherwise BuildNaturalKey. Safe for names with no digits (key is the lowered name).

Function: ImageSortService.NameKeyComparer.public int Compare(NameKey x, NameKey y)
Rationale: Reference-equal names are equal, null sorts first, otherwise key compare OrdinalIgnoreCase (keys already lowered) then name OrdinalIgnoreCase then Ordinal: consistent total order matching ManagedNaturalComparer.Compare. Test: ManagedNaturalComparerEquivalenceTests, NaturalSortPropertyTests.

Function: ImageSortService.public static List<string> Sort( IEnumerable<string> files, ImageSortMode mode, INaturalComparer? naturalComparer = null, ILog? log = null)
Rationale: String-path sort used only by tests (no production caller found, production uses SortEntries). Size modes stat every file (FileInfo.Length) once per key, errors give -1; fine for the oracle role. Tests: ImageSortServiceTests.
Static local Path.GetFileName(path); same semantics as the entry variant.
OrderByDescending key GetFileSize(path, log): evaluated once per element by OrderBy.
OrderBy key GetFileSize(path, log); missing files sort as -1 and log an error per missing file (noise only).

Function: ImageSortService.public static List<string> Sort( IEnumerable<string> files, string? mode, INaturalComparer? naturalComparer = null, ILog? log = null)
Rationale: Maps legacy strings case-insensitively (SIZE and SIZEDESCENDING to SizeDescending, unknown or null to Name); no throw on null. No production caller found; kept for old settings text. Test: ImageSortServiceTests.

Function: ImageSortService.private static long GetFileSize(string path, ILog? log)
Rationale: FileInfo.Length throws FileNotFoundException for a missing file, caught by catch-all and mapped to -1 with a log line; also swallows OperationCanceled/UnauthorizedAccess which is acceptable for a sort key. Only used by the string Sort overload.

Volatile reference write of the latest load task (null clears); only the UI-thread folder load calls it. Test: FolderLoadCoordinatorTests.LatestExplorer (LoadAsync_ExplorerSort_PublishesSnapshotToLatestExplorerSnapshot, LoadAsync_AppDecidedSort_ClearsLatestExplorerSnapshot); no Core-level test.

Reads the volatile field once into a pattern variable (no tearing between check and use) and only returns Result for a successfully completed task, so Result cannot block or throw; faulted/cancelled/running give null. Covered by the App test above.

Function: ManagedNaturalComparer.public int Compare(string? x, string? y)
Rationale: Null ordering first; keys built into stackalloc (<=256 chars) or ArrayPool buffers returned in finally; natural key compare then OrdinalIgnoreCase then Ordinal gives a deterministic total order (a01 vs a1 equal keys fall to ordinal). Non-ASCII digits are treated as digits (char.IsDigit) but only ASCII 0 is trimmed: consistent in KeyLength/WriteKey so no buffer mismatch. Production uses Windows StrCmpLogicalW in App DI while catalog sort uses this one; equivalence between the two is not asserted here. Tests: ManagedNaturalComparerTests, ManagedNaturalComparerEquivalenceTests, NaturalSortPropertyTests.
Empty/null name returns empty; string.Create with exact KeyLength so no overflow or trailing garbage. Tests: ManagedNaturalComparerEquivalenceTests (against NaturalKeyReference).
Static lambda delegating to WriteKey (static, no capture).
Counts one char per non-digit and 10+significant digits+1 per digit run, mirroring WriteKey exactly (all-zero run has no significant digits: length 11); int cannot overflow for filename-length input.

Function: ManagedNaturalComparer.private static int SignificantDigits(string name, int start, int end)
Rationale: Skips leading ASCII 0 only; consistent with WriteKey's trimming loop, so an all-zero run yields 0 digits and prefix 0000000000.

Function: ManagedNaturalComparer.private static void WriteKey(string name, Span<char> destination)
Rationale: Writes lower-invariant non-digits, 10-wide zero-padded digit count then digits then NUL terminator per run; the count prefix makes a2 sort before a10; NUL terminator keeps a1 before a1b. Destination size is exactly KeyLength so no index overflow; rented arrays are only read in [0,length). Tests: ManagedNaturalComparerEquivalenceTests, NaturalSortPropertyTests.

Volatile.Write of Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId; rebinding from another thread silently moves ownership (intended for the composition root). In Release the owner id is only recorded. Test: Bound_MutatedOnOwnerThread_DoesNotThrow, Bound_MutatedFromOtherThread_ThrowsOnlyInDebug.

Conditional(DEBUG) so Release elides every call; owner 0 means unbound (tests) and is unchecked; mismatching thread throws InvalidOperationException naming the member. Mutators Reset/UpdateMetadata/SetCurrent/Remove/Restore/RestoreMembers/ReplaceOrder/RemovePaths all call it; the lazy-mutating reads (IndexOf/Find/Paths) deliberately do not (see W2-CC-08). Tests: ReviewCatalogThreadGuardTests (4).
_entries.Count; cheap, valid on empty catalog. Test: EmptyCatalog_PropertiesAndBoundaries.

Bounds-checked: CurrentIndex outside [0,Count) yields null instead of throwing, so a stale index after concurrent mutation cannot crash the getter; empty catalog gives null. Test: EmptyCatalog_PropertiesAndBoundaries.

Cached string[] rebuilt after structural change (Remove clears _pathsCache, Restore/Reset/ReplaceOrder/RemovePaths via InvalidateIndex); UpdateMetadata does not change paths so the cache stays valid. Cached array is exposed as IReadOnlyList so a caller can only mutate it via an explicit cast. Test: Paths_TakenBeforeAChange_IsNotMutatedByIt; a randomised differential run (3 pair modes x 300 rounds x 60 ops incl. groups) found Paths always equal to the entries.
Lambda e => e.Path projecting to the cached array; entries are never null (Reset filters).

Direct _entries[index].Path; out-of-range index throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException (callers check against Count; MainViewModel.CurrentHasComparePair guards CurrentIndex). No allocation. Covered via many App tests; no direct Core test of the throwing path.

Blank returns -1; lazy EnsureIndex then dictionary lookup; with pending deferred removals the stored position is corrected by BinarySearch over the sorted removed list (removed paths give -1, others stored minus count of removed below). Group members resolve to their entry; first occurrence wins for case-variant duplicates. Verified by a scratch differential run (no violations) and by Index_StaysCorrect_AgainstListModel, Remove_PastThreshold_StillCorrect.

Rebuild is correct (first occurrence wins, group members added unless same as entry path, duplicate flag set when TryAdd fails). It mutates _indexByPath/_removedPositions from a method reachable by IndexOf/Find without AssertOwnerThread; test Bound_ReadFromOtherThread_DoesNotThrow documents that reads are allowed off-thread (comment says preload snapshot) so a concurrent rebuild plus UI mutation would corrupt the Dictionary. I found no production off-thread caller (PreloadScheduler invokes the snapshot delegate synchronously on the UI thread per ADR 0005) so this is unproven. See W2-CC-08.

Marks the index dirty, drops the paths cache and bumps StructuralVersion; every structural mutator except the deferred Remove path calls it. UpdateMetadata intentionally does not (see UpdateMetadata finding W2-CC-04).

Function: ReviewCatalog.public void Reset(IEnumerable<CatalogEntry> entries, RawPairMode rawPairMode, IEnumerable<string>? sidecarPaths = null)
Rationale: Checked: filters null/blank entries, materialises before Clear so an enumeration that reads the catalog or throws leaves the old state intact (tests Reset_PathsEnumerationThrows_KeepsPreviousState, Reset_EntriesEnumerationThrows_KeepsPreviousState), undefined mode throws in GroupEntries before any mutation, CurrentIndex reset to 0 or -1, mode remembered for later restores (Reset_*OverloadForgetsThePreviousPairMode). Duplicate case-variant paths are kept (index first-wins).
Lambda e is not null and Path not blank; keeps Reset total for sloppy callers. Test: Reset_SkipsNullAndBlank.
Delegates to IndexOf then indexes _entries; returns null when absent or blank. Finds a grouped entry by any image member (needed by FileActionController.group lookups).

Function: ReviewCatalog.public bool UpdateMetadata(string path, long length, DateTime lastWriteUtc, int? width = null, int? height = null)
Rationale: Correct on its own: returns false for unknown path and for a non-representative member of a capture (stat belongs to one file; tests UpdateMetadata_PathOfANonRepresentativeMember_IsANoOp, UpdateMetadata_PathOfTheRepresentative_StampsTheGroupEntry); owner thread asserted; WithMetadata keeps dims when unchanged. Concern: it replaces the entry (new Length/LastWriteUtc) without bumping StructuralVersion although EntriesSnapshot (preload) copies those stats, so a running preload keeps the stale stat for the entry until the next structural change (traced only, impact limited to preload cache-key mismatch/wasted decode). See W2-CC-04.

Accepts -1 only for an empty catalog and [0,Count) otherwise; rejects out-of-range and -1 on a non-empty catalog by returning false without change (callers like FolderLoadCoordinator SetCurrent(0) on empty get false). Owner thread asserted. Test: EmptyCatalog_PropertiesAndBoundaries.

Checked both branches: deferred path records the stored position in sorted _removedPositions (binary search insertion) and skips an O(n) rebuild, but only when no duplicate keys exist and fewer than 64 pending removals; otherwise full invalidate. Next-current: removing before current shifts index down, after keeps it, removing current picks min(removedIndex, Count-1), empty gives -1; unknown path returns CurrentIndex unchanged. Removing by a non-representative member removes the whole capture entry (by design). StructuralVersion and Paths cache updated in both branches. Differential run over random Remove/Restore/RestoreMembers/RemovePaths/ReplaceOrder with groups found no index or CurrentIndex violation. Tests: Remove_Burst_DoesNotRebuildIndexPerRemoval, Remove_PastThreshold_StillCorrect, Remove_AfterTheMaximumNumberOfIncrementalRemovals_ForcesAnIndexRebuild, Remove_EntryWhoseMemberPathIsAlsoAnotherEntry_KeepsFindingTheSurvivorByThatPath, Remove_EntryBeforeCurrent_KeepsSameCurrentPath, RandomOperations_MatchReferenceModel.

Function: ReviewCatalog.public bool Restore(string path, int index)
Rationale: Blank and already-listed paths (including group members via IndexOf) rejected; index clamped to [0,Count]; CurrentIndex follows the displayed image (increments when inserted at or before it, set when catalog was empty). Inserted entry is a bare CatalogEntry (no stat/group) which is intended for plain restores; capture restores go through RestoreMembers. Tests: Restore_ClampsIndexAndPreventsDuplicates, Restore_BlankPath_Rejected.

Function: ReviewCatalog.public bool RestoreMembers(IEnumerable<string> paths, int index, CaptureGroup? group = null, bool rawEnabled = true)

Rationale: Uses Directory.EnumerateDirectories(parent) which, with its default (compatible) options, includes Hidden and System directories (reproduced: a hidden .hid sibling is returned), so sibling navigation can land in tool folders such as a hidden thumbnails folder; parent null (root) returns empty; UnauthorizedAccess/IOException logged and mapped to empty (test SiblingFolders_ParentCannotBeListed_ReturnsEmptyAndLogsTheError); GetFullPath throws for null/blank input (callers validate). Function: ExifInfoFieldsJsonConverter.public override ExifInfoFields Read(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options)
Rationale: Number is masked to All (unknown bits dropped), string parsed with Enum.TryParse ignoreCase and masked, other tokens skipped and replaced by Default, null handled (verified: null gives Default, "0" gives None). Leniency defects (reproduced in a scratch run): -1 yields All (every bit set rather than an error), and one unknown name in a list ("FileName, Foo") resets the whole value to Default instead of keeping the valid names, silently with no repair record unlike SettingsEnumConverter. Tests: Settings/ExifInfoSettingsTests, LenientEnumRobustnessTests. See W2-CC-03.

Function: ExifInfoFieldsJsonConverter.public override void Write(Utf8JsonWriter writer, ExifInfoFields value, JsonSerializerOptions options)
Rationale: Writes (value and All).ToString(), which for an exact match emits the composite alias names All or Default (verified: Default serialises as the string Default, All as All) instead of explicit flag names, so the persisted meaning follows future changes of those constants (ModifiedDate was already added after release). Round trip itself is correct. Null writer throws. See W2-CC-03.

mode is not (Default or NameAscending or NameDescending): Name, SizeDescending, SizeAscending and any undefined numeric value use the Explorer order; consistent with the enum docs. Test: ImageSortServiceTests (SortModePolicy cases).
Chains to the one-arg ctor with default(T) (the enum zero member), which is what [JsonConverter(typeof(LenientEnumConverter<T>))] attribute instantiation needs. Test: LenientEnumConverterTests.
Stores the fallback; no validation needed (any T). Used by SettingsEnumConverter with an undefined sentinel. Test: LenientEnumConverterTests.

Function: LenientEnumConverter.public override T Read(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options)
Rationale: String goes through ParseText (case-insensitive, aliases, numeric text), Number only when it fits int and is defined (a flags combination or float falls back to the default), Null and structural tokens return the default after Skip so the reader ends on the value's last token and the surrounding document keeps parsing. Enum.IsDefined(typeof(T), int) is valid because every enum using it has an int underlying type (checked: no byte/long enums in Model). Tests: LenientEnumConverterTests (17), LenientEnumRobustnessTests, LenientEnumNumericStringTests.

Function: LenientEnumConverter.public override void Write(Utf8JsonWriter writer, T value, JsonSerializerOptions options)
Rationale: Writes ToText(value) as a string (undefined numeric values come out as their number text); null writer throws. Test: LenientEnumConverterTests (write/round trip cases).

Function: LenientEnumConverter.public override T ReadAsPropertyName(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options)
Rationale: Needed for Dictionary<DecoderBackend,long> keys; unknown keys map to the default value so two unknown keys collapse into one dictionary slot (metrics only, no user data). Null reader string is handled by ParseText. Test: LenientEnumRobustnessTests/LenientEnumConverterTests dictionary-key cases.

Function: LenientEnumConverter.public override void WriteAsPropertyName(Utf8JsonWriter writer, T value, JsonSerializerOptions options)
Rationale: Writes the property name with ToText so the key text matches Write (InitialViewMode would become 100% etc.); null writer throws.

Blank gives default; trimmed text looked up in the case-insensitive table (names plus aliases), then an invariant-culture int parse that must be defined; anything else gives default. Culture-safe (InvariantCulture). Tests: LenientEnumNumericStringTests, LenientEnumConverterTests.

InitialViewMode maps to the legacy Fit/100%/200%/400% spellings (only those four; FitWidth etc. fall to ToString which equals the alias-less name plus the JsonAlias reads back); every other enum writes its name; undefined values write their number which Read accepts only if defined (SettingsEnumConverter sentinel is normalised before save).

Reflects public static fields once per closed generic type (static initialiser, thread-safe), registers the field name and each non-blank trimmed JsonAlias OrdinalIgnoreCase; an alias that equals another member name overwrites it (no such collision exists today). Test: LenientEnumConverterTests alias cases (PortraitFirst, Size, 100%).

Function: TitleBarFieldsJsonConverter.public override TitleBarFields Read(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options)
Rationale: Same lenient parsing as ExifInfoFields: number masked against All (-1 gives All), strings via Enum.TryParse so a single misspelled name resets the whole title to Default silently, other tokens skipped to Default. See W2-CC-03. Test: Settings/TitleBarFieldsSettingsTests.

Function: TitleBarFieldsJsonConverter.public override void Write(Utf8JsonWriter writer, TitleBarFields value, JsonSerializerOptions options)
Rationale: (value and All).ToString() emits composite alias names (All) or, because Default and FolderName share the value 1, one of two alias names chosen by the runtime (observed FolderName today) so the persisted text is not guaranteed stable across runtimes; both parse back to the same value. See W2-CC-03.
